en: Title: *Saptajinastava* (Hymn to the Seven Victors) Author: Unknown Source: Staël-Holstein 1913, pp. 82–84 (reconstructed from a Chinese transcription)
To the Teacher of the World, worshipped by the realms of gods and men, skilled in compassion, and the instructor of the welfare and liberation of others;
I pay homage to Vipaśyin, the Tathāgata who has reached the state of the Sugatas and has crossed to the further shore of the great flood of the three realms of existence.
[2] Having observed the world sinking in this ocean of existence which has no further shore,
he by whom the Dharma was revealed for the sake of its welfare—
Homage be to that Jina Śikhin!
I pay homage to the Buddha Viśvabhū, whose splendor surpasses that of the moon and sun, and who,
like the unfathomable flood of the ocean, is profound in wisdom and discipline.
[4] He whose fame, resembling the rays of the moon,
adorns and illuminates this earth—
him, who is as rare as the flower of the Udumbara tree, [I praise].
I pay homage to Krakucchanda, the great Lord of Sages.
By him who, with a mind that is expansive, free from stain, dispassionate, and ever-acting for the welfare of others,
has destroyed darkness and is devoid of impurity— him [I worship].
I bow to Kanakamuni, who is honored by the gods.
[6] Whose radiant splendor was fair with the rays of molten gold and possessed a brilliance more intense than a thousand suns;
the Supreme Being, who is to be venerated by all people.
I pay homage to him whose name is Kāśyapa.
Having awakened the world with the nets of rays of his speech, like the sun’s rays awakening a cluster of lotuses,
the lamp of Śākyamuni has entered into nirvāṇa.
Homage to that Teacher, who is supremely compassionate.
[8] But he named Maitreya, who dwells in the Tuṣita abode and whose enlightenment is indeed separated by only one birth—
he who will arise as a Sugata upon the earth.
With my whole being, I bow down to him.
[9] Having praised the seven Victors of the past and the eighth Bodhisattva of the future, whatever immeasurable merit has been acquired by me—
By that, may all sentient beings be free from affliction.
The *Saptajinastava* is completed.
